title: Astronaut Photos Taken Just 13 Years Apart Show a Major Shift in City Lights - Nautilus
gist: Paywalled teaser. NASA astronaut Don Pettit's orbital photos taken about 13 years apart show cities around the world switching from orange sodium vapor lighting to white LED lamps over roughly 15 years. The comparisons cover Miami, Chicago, Las Vegas, Seoul, São Paulo, Hong Kong and Mexico City.

insights.claim: Over roughly the last 15 years, city lighting has shifted on a large scale from orange sodium vapor lamps to white LED lamps.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Confirms how far LED street-lighting retrofits have penetrated, which matters for lighting vendors and municipal energy-efficiency savings.
insights.quote: there’s been a huge shift in the way our cities are lit
insights.locator: Over the last 15 years or so

insights.claim: Don Pettit's before-and-after orbital photos show the change from sodium to LED lighting in Miami, Chicago, Las Vegas, Seoul, São Paulo, Hong Kong and Mexico City, with stark differences.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: The transition spans developed and emerging-market cities, so it is global and not regional.

insights.claim: Astronaut photography from orbit can track changes in urban infrastructure over time.
insights.speaker: David Nield
insights.so_what: Night-light imagery works as alternative data on urbanization, electrification and infrastructure upgrades.
insights.quote: document the global shift from orange sodium vapor lighting to white LED
